title: Iterative Fiber Depth-First Walker
concept: Non-Recursive Tree Traversal via Fiber Pointers
problemStatement: Implement `walkFiberTree(root, onVisit)` that visits every node in a Fiber tree in depth-first order using ONLY `child`, `sibling`, and `return` without recursion or array stacks.
interviewTrap: Using recursion will overflow the call stack when React reconciles large DOM trees of 10,000+ nodes.

testCases.name: Traverses root and children in pre-order
testCases.testFn: const root = { id: 'Root', child: null, sibling: null, return: null }; const a = { id: 'A', child: null, return: root }; const b = { id: 'B', child: null, sibling: null, return: root }; root.child = a; a.sibling = b; const visited = []; walkFiberTree(root, f => visited.push(f.id)); return visited;

testCases.name: Navigates multi-level nested children
testCases.testFn: const root = { id: 'Root', child: null, return: null }; const b = { id: 'B', child: null, sibling: null, return: root }; const a1 = { id: 'A1', child: null, sibling: null }; const a = { id: 'A', child: a1, sibling: b, return: root }; a1.return = a; root.child = a; const visited = []; walkFiberTree(root, f => visited.push(f.id)); return visited;

testCases.name: Handles leaf node with no children gracefully
testCases.testFn: const node = { id: 'OnlyOne', child: null, sibling: null, return: null }; const visited = []; walkFiberTree(node, f => visited.push(f.id)); return visited;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: React reconciles component trees using an iterative Depth-First Search (DFS) walker through `child`, `sibling`, and `return` pointers. This eliminates recursive function calls, enabling the work loop to pause at any node and resume later.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 2. If `current.child !== null`, descend: `current = current.child` and continue loop.
3. If no child, we complete the work (completeWork phase). While `current !== null`:
a. If `current.sibling !== null`, traverse laterally: `current = current.sibling` and break to step 1.
b. Otherwise, ascend up to parent: `current = current.return`.
c. If we return to root or above, terminate.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: This algorithm is the exact core of React's `workLoopSync` and `workLoopConcurrent` (`packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberWorkLoop.js`). `beginWork` descends down `child` pointers, and `completeWork` bubbles up `return` pointers while pivoting across `sibling` pointers.

complexity.time: O(N) visiting each fiber node in the tree exactly twice (once on descent, once on ascent).
complexity.space: O(1) auxiliary call stack space (strictly iterative pointer traversal).

edgeCasesHandled: Single root node without children returns `[root]`.
Deep unbalanced trees traverse without call stack overflow.
Multi-child sibling chains traverse in correct left-to-right order.

specifications: Lin Clark's A Cartoon Intro to Fiber (DFS work traversal explanation)
verifiedRules: Child pointer is visited first; if absent, sibling is visited; if absent, return pointer is ascended.
The traversal is strictly O(1) in call stack memory.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Explain the exact order of traversal in React's work loop: beginWork vs completeWork.
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: 1) `beginWork`: React descends depth-first down `fiber.child` pointers, calling component render functions and reconciling children until it reaches a leaf node (a fiber with `child === null`). 2) `completeWork`: at the leaf, React creates/updates the real host DOM node and bubbles up effect flags. If `fiber.sibling` exists, React pivots to the sibling and restarts `beginWork`. If no sibling, it bubbles up to `fiber.return`, completes the parent, and checks the parent's sibling.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: The #1 core algorithm question asked in senior/staff React engine interviews.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why does completeWork run bottom-up while beginWork runs top-down?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Because a parent DOM element cannot append its child DOM nodes until the children have been created! `beginWork` runs top-down to determine what needs to be rendered, but `completeWork` runs bottom-up so leaf DOM nodes are created and appended to parent DOM nodes, assembling the DOM subtree before the commit phase.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of host tree construction and mutation batching.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does the iterative loop achieve O(1) auxiliary call stack space?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Standard tree recursion allocates a C++ stack frame for every depth level (O(D) call stack). Fiber's `workLoop` is a single `while (workInProgress !== null)` loop where navigation is executed via simple pointer assignments (`workInProgress = workInProgress.child` or `sibling` or `return`). The Call Stack depth remains constant at 1.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests computer science algorithmic efficiency principles.

realWorldUseCases.description: The core `workLoopConcurrent` in React source code traversing components while honoring time-slicing frame deadlines.

howToExplain.opening: React reconciles components using an iterative Depth-First Search with beginWork on the descent and completeWork on the ascent.
keyPoints: beginWork descends down child pointers, evaluating components.
completeWork ascends up return pointers, building DOM instances.
sibling pointers allow lateral tree traversal without recursion.
Operates in O(N) time with O(1) call stack memory.
howToExplain.closingImpression: This two-pass descent-ascent traversal allows React to construct fully assembled DOM subtrees before committing to the screen in one unified batch.
analogies: A zipper: beginWork unzips down to inspect the teeth (children); completeWork zips back up, locking the assembled pieces in place.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming DOM nodes are attached to the document body during completeWork.
commonMistakes.why: completeWork only creates DOM nodes and attaches them to parent DOM nodes in memory (in-memory subtree). The actual insertion into the live document happens during the synchronous Commit Phase.
commonMistakes.correct: Clarify that live DOM insertion is strictly deferred to commitMutationEffects.

followUpDeepDive.question: What is subtreeFlags and how does it optimize completeWork bubbling?
followUpDeepDive.answer: In React 18+, `subtreeFlags` is a 32-bit bitmask on each fiber that aggregates all pending mutations of its descendants. When bubbling up in `completeWork`, `parent.subtreeFlags |= (child.flags | child.subtreeFlags)`. If a parent's `subtreeFlags === 0`, React can skip scanning the entire subtree during the commit phase in O(1) time.
